title: Housing Price Prediction Model

blocks.text: Housing Price Prediction Model
Project Brief for Responsible AI Review
Version 0.2 | Development stage

Division or section | Economic Analysis Division
Project manager | Eljo Example
Primary contact | Jordan Lee
Reviewer | Moe Example
Intended users | Internal Statistics Canada analysts
Project Overview

This project develops supervised machine learning models to predict residential property prices using historical housing market data. The project is currently in development and is intended for internal analytical use. The system produces numeric price predictions rather than free-text output.
Project type: classical supervised machine learning Lifecycle status: development Output: numeric price prediction Primary users: internal analysts
Technical Approach
The team evaluates several model families and trains models from scratch using internal datasets.
Linear Regression Random Forest XGBoost

The current implementation uses open-source Python libraries. The project does not use generative AI, large language models, AI agents, information retrieval, fine-tuning, third-party models, external pretrained models, or foundation models.
Data and Privacy

The project uses historical housing records. Some records may contain personal information linked to specific properties or owners. The project does not use sensitive attributes or confidential data, and no third-party data sources are currently included.
Model outputs are numeric, but the team is reviewing whether record-level predictions could be linked back to identifiable information.

Area | Current status | Open question
Data | Internal housing records identified | Can records be linked to identifiable individuals?
Output | Numeric record-level predictions | Is output linkage possible?
Privacy | Personal information may exist | Which privacy controls apply?
Deployment and Oversight
The project is planned for internal operational deployment after testing and review. Human oversight is required before predictions are used.

The model may support analytical decisions. The model does not make fully automated decisions. The project does not interact directly with members of the public or external clients. Monitoring and retraining procedures need to be defined before launch.
Governance Considerations
Current governance considerations include:

Documenting model limitations and intended use. Assessing whether housing variables may act as proxies for protected characteristics. Reviewing output linkage and re-identification risks. Defining monitoring and retraining procedures before deployment.

Area | Current status | Open question
Deployment | Internal deployment is planned | Which monitoring controls are required?
Decision support | Predictions may inform analysis | Which operational decisions, if any, rely on output?
Procurement | Not specified | Are vendors or external services involved?
